def: The rule that confidential communications made to obtain legal advice cannot be compelled as evidence, and which can be lost if confidentiality is lost.
Protection against disclosure of materials a lawyer prepares in anticipation of litigation.
A rule or system barrier that keeps a team away from a matter because of a conflict of interest; also called an information barrier.
A set of preferred positions and fallback terms against which a lawyer or tool compares the clauses of a contract under review.
Document review in which a classifier trained on lawyers' labels ranks or labels the remaining documents for relevance.
The documents a review process discards without human review, which are sampled to estimate what relevant material was missed.
The proportion of relevant documents found in a random sample of the null set, used to estimate how many relevant documents the review left behind.
The sequence of checks for a legal citation: existence, identity, quotation, good law and finally whether the case supports the proposition.
A legal authority that has not been overruled, reversed or materially limited by later decisions, checked with a citator service.
